history.cultural: The game holds cultural significance in Navajo communities as a social activity that brings people together. It is often played at gatherings and serves as an intergenerational activity where elders teach younger members. The mathematical aspect (making tens) reflects the value placed on mental agility.
history.evolution: Originally played with traditional materials, the game adapted to use standard playing cards as they became available. The core mechanic of making tens has remained consistent, though regional variations exist in scoring and special combinations.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. Cards have numerical values: A=1, 2-10=face value, J=Q=K=10.
setup.dealing: Four cards dealt to each player, and four cards placed face-up in the center layout. Remaining cards form the draw pile.

rules.objective: Capture the most cards by making combinations that sum to 10. Special combinations may have higher values.
rules.gameplay: 1. On your turn, play one card from your hand. 2. Capture cards from the center that combine with your played card to make 10 (e.g., play a 7, capture a 3). 3. Multiple cards can be captured if their sum equals the played card's complement to 10. 4. If you cannot capture, your card is added to the center layout. 5. After playing, draw a card to replenish your hand. 6. When the draw pile is exhausted, play out remaining hands.
keyRules: Multiple cards can be captured in one play if they sum correctly
If no capture possible, card is added to center layout
Replenish hand after each play until draw pile is empty

strategy.basic: Look for simple pairings that make 10 (1+9, 2+8, 3+7, 4+6, 5+5). Remember which cards have been played and which remain in the draw pile.
strategy.intermediate: Plan multiple captures when possibleâ€”if you have a 10 and the center has 3+4+3, you can capture all three. Block opponents by playing cards that don't help them make 10.
strategy.advanced: Track all cards played to predict what opponents hold. Set up combinations that force opponents to leave you good captures. Manage your hand to have flexible capture options.
tips: Remember that face cards (J, Q, K) all equal 10 and can capture a 10 from the center
The 5 is the most flexible card since 5+5=10â€”save it for when two 5s are in the center
Watch what your opponents capture to deduce what they might be holding
